summary: Chelan County, WA ridge-top site of an L-4 cab built in 1933 and taken down in 1970; the Poe Mountain Trail reaches it inside Glacier Peak Wilderness.

facts.status_note: The cab came down in 1970; sources differ on whether it was removed or destroyed. Willhite's photos show a footing, an eye bolt and an anchor rod.

access.note: Hiking trail inside Glacier Peak Wilderness; wilderness regulations apply.

visit.trail_note: Poe Mountain Trail from the Little Wenatchee Ford Trailhead. Willhite lists 3 miles and 2,000 feet of gain, and advises higher clearance on the access road.

events.note: Marshall Stenerson named as the Poe Mountain lookout-fireman in June 1933
Donald Reed Theoe was the lookout, per Willhite
Register says removed; FireLookout.com and Willhite say destroyed
Registered October 28, 2012 as US 1418, WA 318; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1970; FireLookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1970. The year agrees across sources; the story gives both words.

notes_for_editor: Gain figures differ: Willhite gives 2,000 feet over 3 miles, while the Forest Service page says the trail gains nearly 1,000 feet per mile; the routes may differ, so the story gives Willhite's figures only as his. Trailhead names differ: the Forest Service names Little Wenatchee Ford Trailhead, and a Willhite photo caption names Irving Pass Trailhead; not reconciled and not in the story. Staffing: 1957 is the last staffing found, and the 'no longer staffed' status is our reading since no source says it in those words. The 1933 Stenerson item is quoted by Forest Lookouts from The Leavenworth Echo; the newspaper itself was not read. The record's federal ownership and gone status match the sources, so no corrections. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 5 page reads.
